_comment: What each room's blaster knows how to send. THE LIVE COPY IS NOT IN THE
REPO and is not in /config either: the gateway writes this file itself,
every time a code is learned off a remote or confirmed as working, so it
is state rather than configuration. It lives at
/home/homestack/home-lab/state/home-voice/ir-codes.json on compute,
which docker-compose.yml mounts writable at /state.
This example exists to document the shape. You should never need to write
one by hand — say 'Alfred, aprende el botón de encender de la tele' and
point the remote at the puck.
A command has one of three shapes, and all three replay:
protocol + code + bits   a remote the library recognises. Most of them.
protocol + state         an air conditioner: the whole state in one
frame, because there is no 'warmer' button on
the wire, only 'cool, 23, fan auto, on'.
raw + khz                timings, for a remote nothing recognised. Still
perfectly sendable; it just cannot be reasoned
about, so 'a bit warmer' is not available.
`ac_protocol` on a device is the better way to run an air conditioner:
with it set, POST /v1/ir/send {ac:{...}} builds any state on demand, so a
temperature nobody ever captured still works. Stored commands are the
fallback for a unit the library cannot encode.
`confirmed` is whether a person actually watched it work. A code from a
web lookup starts false and is set true once somebody says the television
turned on. Both are sendable; the flag is there so Alfred can say 'creo
que es este' instead of 'este es'.
